And, back to the original problem, how a missing ground prong can be dangerous, I recall this accident:

A 12 year boy at a public pool got out of the pool, dripping wet, to purchase a soda from a vending machine. Upon touching the vending machine, he collapsed on the ground. 911 was called, attempts to revive him were unsuccessful. He died of cardiac arrest.

Investigation revealed that the ground prong on the vending machine's power cord was missing. Additionally, the power cord had been pierced by one of the vending machine's legs such that the insulation was broken and the metal leg was making contact with the hot wire. The vending machine was not plugged into a GFCI.

This caused the metal frame of the vending machine to become energized and remain energized.

Had the ground prong not been missing, the circuit breaker would have tripped, because it would have provided a good solid path to ground sufficient to trip a breaker. Had a GFCI (breaker or outlet or in-line portable type) been present, it would have tripped, because the GFCI would have sensed more than 5mA of leakage to ground.
